kangaroo-ca-2014-g1112-03.title: Try the squares
kangaroo-ca-2014-g1112-03.body:
The squares below 100 are $1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81$. The only two that add up to 100 are $36 + 64$, so $\{a, b\} = \{6, 8\}$ and $a + b = 14$.

**Answer: (E) 14**

kangaroo-ca-2014-g1112-03.title: Scale a Pythagorean triple
kangaroo-ca-2014-g1112-03.body:
$a^2 + b^2 = 10^2$ means $(a, b, 10)$ is a Pythagorean triple; the only one with hypotenuse 10 is $2\cdot(3, 4, 5) = (6, 8, 10)$. So $a + b = 14$.

**Answer: (E) 14**

kangaroo-ca-2014-g1112-10.title: Area with the sine
kangaroo-ca-2014-g1112-10.body:
If the angle between the two sides of length 2 is $\theta$, the area is $\frac12\cdot 2\cdot 2\cdot\sin\theta = 2\sin\theta \le 2$, with equality for $\theta = 90^\circ$ (a right isosceles triangle with legs 2).

**Answer: (B) 2**

kangaroo-ca-2014-g1112-10.title: Base and height
kangaroo-ca-2014-g1112-10.body:
Take one side of length 2 as the base. The other side of length 2 starts at an end of the base, so the height is at most 2 (when it is perpendicular). So the area is at most $\frac12\cdot 2\cdot 2 = 2$, reached by the right isosceles triangle.

**Answer: (B) 2**

kangaroo-ca-2014-g1112-19.title: Examples and a case check

kangaroo-ca-2014-g1112-20.title: Last digits
kangaroo-ca-2014-g1112-20.body:
The last digits of $2^n$ repeat with period 4: $2, 4, 8, 6$ for $n \equiv 1, 2, 3, 0 \pmod 4$. $2^n + 1$ is divisible by 5 when it ends in 5 (or 0), i.e. when $2^n$ ends in 4: $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$. Of $100, \dots, 104$, only $102$ works: $2^{102}$ ends in 4, so $2^{102} + 1$ ends in 5.

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-ca-2014-g1112-26.title: Binomial count
kangaroo-ca-2014-g1112-26.body:
From each box the ball is red with probability $\frac14$. Choose which 2 of the 3 boxes give red ($3$ ways); then the probability is $\frac14\cdot\frac14\cdot\frac34 = \frac{3}{64}$ for each choice. Total: $3\cdot\frac{3}{64} = \frac{9}{64}$.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-ca-2014-g1112-26.title: Count outcomes
kangaroo-ca-2014-g1112-26.body:
There are $4^3 = 64$ equally likely outcomes. Exactly two red: pick the non-red box (3 ways) and its colour (3 ways): $9$ outcomes. Probability $\frac{9}{64}$.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-ca-2014-g1112-27.title: Half-diagonal of the outer square
kangaroo-ca-2014-g1112-27.body:
The inner square has side 1. Each equilateral triangle stands on one of its sides and points outwards to a corner of the outer square. By symmetry, the centre $O$, the midpoint of an inner side and the opposite triangle apex (an outer corner) lie on one line. The distance from $O$ to an inner side is $\frac12$ and the height of the triangle is $\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$, so the outer square's half-diagonal is $\frac{1 + \sqrt3}{2}$, and its diagonal is $1 + \sqrt3$.

Area $= \frac{\text{diagonal}^2}{2} = \frac{(1+\sqrt3)^2}{2} = \frac{4 + 2\sqrt3}{2} = 2 + \sqrt3$.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-ca-2014-g1112-27.title: Cut into pieces
kangaroo-ca-2014-g1112-27.body:
The outer square consists of the inner square (area 1), the four equilateral triangles (area $\frac{\sqrt3}{4}$ each, $\sqrt3$ together) and four more triangles, one along each side of the outer square. Each of these has two sides of length 1 (sides of equilateral triangles) meeting at a vertex of the inner square, with angle $360^\circ - 90^\circ - 60^\circ - 60^\circ = 150^\circ$, so its area is $\frac12\cdot 1\cdot 1\cdot\sin 150^\circ = \frac14$.

Total: $1 + \sqrt3 + 4\cdot\frac14 = 2 + \sqrt3$.

**Answer: (B)**
